title: Activepieces vs Lindy: Pricing and Features (2026)
summary: Activepieces vs Lindy differ in deployment: Lindy is hosted and managed, while Activepieces is self-hosted open-source.
body_markdown:
## Embedding automation inside your own product


If customers need to build or run automations inside your product, an open-source workflow platform offers a route for it: the Embed plan, from $36,000 a year through sales, puts a white-label flow builder, AI agents and 760+ integrations inside your own product.


Lindy is built for your own team to use inside Lindy's app.


That gap shows up the first time a customer asks where their automations live and whose login they need.


### What embedding means


When you embed, your customers never leave your product. They build or switch on automations in your interface, under your branding and your authentication, while the workflow engine runs behind it.


A hosted assistant that your team configures is a different thing: the people using it sign in to the vendor's workspace, not yours.


The test is simple. If a customer would have to create an account with the automation vendor, you have integrated with it, not embedded it.


### Embedding with a self-hostable engine


Because the platform is open source and can be self-hosted, embedding is practical. You can run the engine in your own infrastructure, so customer workflow data stays where your product's data already lives. That matters when a customer's security review asks about subprocessors.


Embedding isn't a self-serve checkbox. It goes through the sales form at[https://www.activepieces.com/sales](https://www.activepieces.com/sales) , where you describe how you want to ship it and get terms for your case.


Plan for that conversation before you commit a roadmap date to it, and ask what's included for your deployment model.


### What Lindy publishes


I found no embedded or white-label offering described in what Lindy publishes. Its material describes assistants that you configure in its hosted app and connect to the tools your team already uses, so the documented path is customers or colleagues working in Lindy's own workspace.


You can still trigger a Lindy assistant from your product by other means, but your customers would be relying on a service they can't see into or branded as yours.


For shipping automation to your customers, the verdict is the open-source platform. For automation only your own staff use, this question doesn't decide anything.
